title: Compound adjectives
subtitle: well-dressed, easy-going, hard-up
summary: Describe people, places and things with two-part adjectives such as curly-haired, absent-minded, well-off and time-consuming.

lesson.heading: Form and meaning
lesson.text: A compound adjective has two parts and is usually written with a hyphen. Its meaning is normally clear from the two words put together. The second part is often a present participle in **-ing** or a past participle in **-ed**.

examples.text: a **well-dressed** man, but: He is always **well dressed**.
examples.note: the hyphen is used before a noun but not after a verb

lesson.heading: Personal appearance
lesson.text: Many compound adjectives describe how someone looks. Here is a description that runs from the head downwards.

examples.text: He was wearing an **open-necked** shirt, **brand-new**, **tight-fitting** jeans and **open-toed** sandals.

lesson.heading: Personality and character
rows: always thinking about himself or herself instead of others
thinks he or she is better than other people (informal)

lesson.heading: Compounds ending in a preposition or particle
rows: The workers declared an all-out strike.
Once there were fields here, but now it's a totally built-up area.
That student's parents are very well-off.
He is always complaining of being hard-up.
I love these shoes but they're worn-out.
This area was once prosperous but now looks very run-down.

lesson.heading: Compound adjectives and their usual nouns
rows: train travel (at a less busy time)

lesson.heading: Varying a compound adjective
lesson.text: You can build a family of adjectives by changing just one half of the compound. Learning them in sets is far quicker than learning them one at a time.

examples.note: waterproof is usually written as one word, without a hyphen

lesson.text: *Handmade* furniture is made by hand, *home-made* cake is made at home and a *man-made* lake is made by people - the first half always tells you by whom or by what.

exercises.prompt: Match each compound adjective with its meaning.

pairs.right: thinks he is better than others

exercises.prompt: A problem that never ends is a ___ problem.
exercises.explanation: The second part of a compound adjective is often a present participle.

exercises.prompt: A girl who has long legs is a ___ girl.
exercises.explanation: Body-part compounds take -ed: long-legged, broad-shouldered, blue-eyed.

exercises.prompt: Sandals whose toes are open are ___ sandals.
exercises.explanation: Compare open-necked shirt and open-toed sandals.

exercises.prompt: A person who is very relaxed and kind is an easy-going, ___ person.
A shirt whose neck is open and which fits tightly is an ___ shirt.
exercises.explanation: The -ed form goes with the body part and the -ing form with the way it fits.

exercises.prompt: A boy who dresses well and is brown from the sun is a ___ boy.
exercises.explanation: Well-dressed and suntanned both use a past participle.

exercises.prompt: It was an old, ___ hotel that needed modernising.
exercises.explanation: Run-down means in a very bad condition.

exercises.prompt: None of the rooms were ___ , so it was very hot at night.
exercises.explanation: Air-conditioned rooms have cooled, controlled air.

exercises.prompt: The ___ restaurant was really just a coffee bar.
exercises.explanation: So-called suggests the name is not deserved.

exercises.prompt: It's a very ___ coast, with hotels and villas everywhere.
exercises.explanation: A built-up area is covered with buildings.

exercises.prompt: ___ train travel is much cheaper than travelling at busy times.
exercises.explanation: Off-peak means at a time which is less busy.

exercises.prompt: The workers went on ___ strike over a long-standing pay dispute.
exercises.explanation: An all-out strike is a total strike.

exercises.prompt: She used to be quite ___ but she lost a lot of money and now she is always hard-up.
exercises.explanation: Well-off means rich; its opposite here is hard-up, meaning poor.

exercises.prompt: She has to have a sugar-free diet but it's very ___ checking everything she buys.
exercises.explanation: Time-consuming means it takes a great deal of time.

exercises.prompt: Sort these compound adjectives by what they describe.

exercises.statement: The President was driven in a bullet-proof limousine along a route that was top secret.
exercises.explanation: Correct - bullet-proof and top secret are both compound adjectives from this unit.
